description: Ever since we opened our doors in 1707, our Piccadilly flagship has remained the beating heart of Fortnum’s. Founded by William Fortnum and Hugh Mason, we originally started life selling Queen Anne’s leftover candles. Today, we boast five floors of extraordinary things to see, taste and do.

factsheet.heading: Building
paragraphs: What began as a market stall on Duke Street found its permanent home at 182-183 Piccadilly in 1756. As Fortnum's grew, so too did the building, expanding to the footprint it occupies today. The original store was rebuilt in the 1830s and later redesigned in the 1920s by Wimperis, Simpson and Guthrie. In 1964, the now-famous Fortnum's Clock was unveiled, designed by Berkeley Sutcliffe and fitted with bells cast by the Whitechapel Bell Foundry, whose works include both Big Ben and the Liberty Bell.
